match.reason: The bank card 'What human rights are' teaches the four features of human rights, but the new point's brief centres on their historical origins and the 1948 Universal Declaration, which that card does not cover, and those points are taught separately in the bank.

draft.title: What human rights are
card: Human rights are basic rights and freedoms that every person has because they are human. They do not depend on a person's nationality, race, religion or status.
The idea grew out of history. After the Second World War, the world saw the harm done when governments ignored the dignity of people.
In 1948 the United Nations General Assembly adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR). It was the first global statement of the rights all people should have.
The UDHR is a declaration, which sets out shared standards. It is not itself a treaty that binds countries.
draft.remember: Human rights belong to everyone as people, and the UDHR of 1948 set them out.

a.q: Why are human rights described as universal?
opts: Every person has them simply by being human
Every country has agreed to enforce them in court
Every person receives them when they become a citizen
Every person has them once a parliament passes a law
a.why: Human rights belong to people because they are human, whatever their nationality or status. Citizenship is a tempting answer, but the card says rights do not depend on nationality.
a.clue: Think about what a person needs to have these rights.

b.q: Leila says the UDHR in 1948 created human rights for the first time, so no one had them before it. What is the best reply?
opts: The idea grew from history and the UDHR set it out
The UDHR gave rights only to people in member countries
The UDHR was a treaty that gave rights legal force
Rights existed only for people who lived in democracies
b.why: The idea of human rights grew out of history, and the UDHR in 1948 set the rights out in a global statement. It did not create them, and it was a declaration, not a binding treaty.
b.clue: Did the UDHR start the idea, or write it down?

a.best: Every person has them simply by being human

b.best: The idea grew from history and the UDHR set it out
